prompt: Customers receive automatic email notifications when out-of-stock products are restocked, and the merchant can view all signups and sent notifications in the admin.

intent.desiredOutcome: Customers receive automatic email notifications when out-of-stock products are restocked, and the merchant can view all signups and sent notifications in the admin.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version handles duplicate signups gracefully (one signup per customer per product), avoids sending multiple emails if inventory fluctuates, and shows the merchant clear data: who signed up, which products, when notifications were sent. Edge case: if a product is restocked then goes out of stock again before the email sends, clarify whether to still notify or cancel. The admin panel should be scannable at a glance and let the merchant remove spam or duplicate signups easily.

plan.dataFlow: A customer visits a product page where the storefront widget detects an out-of-stock product and presents a signup form; the customer submits their email and the product reference, which is recorded as a pending signup in the database, deduplicated so each customer-product pair has exactly one active signup. When an inventory restocked event fires, the system queries all pending signups for that product, marks each as notified, and sends each customer an email. The merchant can view all signups and notification history in the admin panel, filtered by product or status, and can delete individual signups. If a product goes back out of stock before emails are dispatched, the send still proceeds since the restock event has been observed.

triggers.event: a product variant's inventory level is restocked from zero to a positive quantity
triggers.idempotency: if a restock event arrives for a product whose pending signups have already been moved to notified by a prior delivery of the same event, treat subsequent deliveries as no-ops

capabilities.description: Record a customer's request to be notified when a specific out-of-stock product is restocked.
Determine whether an active signup already exists for the given customer email and product variant before inserting a new one.
Retrieve all pending signups for a given product variant so notifications can be dispatched.
Retrieve product and variant details needed to populate the notification email.
Send a restock notification email to a customer informing them that the product they requested is available again.
Update the signup record to reflect whether the notification email was successfully sent or failed.
Return a paginated, filterable list of signups and their notification statuses for the merchant admin view.
Allow the merchant to remove a specific signup record from the system.

persistence.name: restock_signups
persistence.purpose: Stores each customer's request to be notified when a specific product variant is restocked, and tracks the lifecycle of that notification.

columns.name: customer_email
columns.purpose: email address the customer wants the notification sent to

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the parent product in the external catalog

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the specific variant the customer is waiting for

columns.name: product_name
columns.purpose: denormalized product title captured at signup time for display in admin

columns.name: variant_name
columns.purpose: denormalized variant title captured at signup time for display in admin

columns.name: signed_up_at
columns.purpose: when the customer submitted the signup

columns.name: notified_at
columns.purpose: when the notification email was successfully dispatched

columns.name: failure_reason
columns.purpose: description of why notification delivery failed, if applicable

persistence.keyedBy: one row per customer email and variant combination; duplicate active signups for the same pair are not permitted

persistence.name: restock_events
persistence.purpose: Records each observed restock event so that duplicate webhook deliveries for the same restock can be detected and suppressed.

columns.name: received_at
columns.purpose: when the restock event was first received

columns.name: processed
columns.purpose: whether signups for this restock have already been dispatched

persistence.keyedBy: one row per restock event, keyed by the variant identifier and a deduplication window

transitions.trigger: restock notification email delivery attempt failed
merchant deletes the signup before notification fires

invariants: exactly one active (pending) signup per customer email and variant pair at any time
a signup in a terminal state never returns to pending
notified_at is set if and only if the signup is in the notified state

externalContracts.purpose: Accept a customer's restock notification signup for an out-of-stock product variant.
Return a paginated list of all signups with their status, filterable by product or status.
Allow the merchant to delete a specific signup record by its identifier.

edgeCases: A customer submits a signup form twice for the same product variant — the second request is rejected as a duplicate and the existing pending signup is preserved.
A product is restocked and immediately oversold before notification emails are dispatched — the system still sends notifications because the restock event was legitimately observed.
The email provider returns a delivery failure for one customer in a batch — that signup is marked failed with the reason recorded, while all other signups in the batch continue to be processed.

A restock webhook is delivered more than once for the same variant within a short window — the restock events table deduplicates processing so customers receive at most one notification per restock cycle.
A customer's email address is malformed at signup — the request is rejected immediately with a validation error and no record is persisted.
The merchant deletes a pending signup before the restock event fires — the signup transitions to cancelled and is excluded from future notification batches.
